title: Adic stratified finite presentations and finite constant local models
statement: Fix a universe $u$ and a prime $\ell$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme in universe $u$, meaning quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring with its specified multiplication and a certificate [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate] of one of the three families $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite. For the algebraic closure use the finite-subextension-valued ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ and $D_X=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Under the section-action equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], a $\Lambda_X$-module $M$ is constructible in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense [def-sfb-constructible-module] if and only if it is constructible in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification $X=\coprod_aX_a$ and on every stratum a pro-étale cover $\{U_{ai}\to X_a\}$ and finitely presented scalar $\Lambda(*)$-modules $P_{ai}$ with $M|_{U_{ai}}\cong\Lambda_{U_{ai}}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_{ai}$. The stratifications on the two sides may differ, and integral torsion scalar modules are allowed. Consequently the bounded constructible full subcategory $\mathcal B_X$ of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] equals $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], as object properties in the same ordinary derived category $D_X$. No derived-completeness condition is imposed.

source.place: Part (2), integral/rational bullets: comparison of the stratified local-presentation and finite constant local-model predicates; extracted from the returned item, step 2. The complete short agent proof with cited nodes is in report.md, under Proof in words for this node.

proof.text: Work with the sectionwise module sheaves corresponding to $M$ under [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Its forward functor keeps the abelian sheaf, sections and restrictions identically; the action is the section action of the same ring multiplication. A finite sum of the regular module therefore corresponds to the same finite free module, and the cokernel universal property is unchanged under this equivalence. For every stratum immersion or covering map $g:V\to X$, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) identifies $g^{-1}\Lambda_X$ with $\Lambda_V$. Its final paragraph identifies module pullback with inverse image equipped with the transported action. Hence a presentation over $g^*\Lambda_X$ in the internal definition is precisely a presentation over $\Lambda_V$ in the sectionwise convention. We use these canonical identifications throughout.

source.place: Restriction paragraph; internal/sectionwise conventions and Cartesian coefficients

proof.text: The assumed local Noetherianity gives quasi-separatedness by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; together with the assumed quasi-compactness this puts $X$ in the qcqs branch of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], descending chains of closed subsets of $X$ stabilize: a minimal member of the set of chain terms equals every later term. Every stratum $S\subseteq X$ also has this property. Indeed, for a descending closed chain $C_n=S\cap F_n$, with $F_n$ closed in $X$, replace $F_n$ by $\bigcap_{j\le n}F_j$; its intersection with $S$ is still $C_n$, and the resulting ambient chain stabilizes. Thus every stratum has Noetherian underlying topology, as required by both field-coefficient local-triviality lemmas below.

source.place: Tags 01OY (lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated) and 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology); elementary subspace descending-chain argument

proof.text: Suppose $M$ has the finite stratification and finite constant local models of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. On each stratum, the last assertion of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] gives local finite presentation: its scalar matrix description is also a finite presentation over the coefficient ring sheaf. With the identifications of step 1, the very same stratification therefore satisfies [def-sfb-constructible-module]. This proves the reverse implication for all three families, including torsion scalar modules.

For $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, apply [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] on $X$ itself, which is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian by assumption. Its conditions (i) and (ii) are exactly the two module predicates here, under step 1. In particular its scalar modules are finitely presented over $\mathcal O_E$, its presentations allow arbitrary coefficient-sheaf entries, and its conclusion allows a changed finite constructible stratification. The implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) gives the required forward implication in the integral case, without requiring the scalar modules to be torsion-free.

source.place: Example 3.1 and Theorem 6.2(2)–(3); the precise local-presentation comparison obligation is the existing integral comparison node

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\underline E$, choose a finite stratification witnessing [def-sfb-constructible-module]. On a stratum $S$, the restriction is locally finitely presented, hence has finite free cokernel presentations on a pro-étale cover by [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. Step 2 supplies Noetherian underlying topology on $S$, so [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality] gives a pro-étale cover $W_j\to S$ with $M|_{W_j}\cong\Lambda_{W_j}^{r_j}$, $r_j\ge0$. Put $P_j=E^{r_j}$. It is finitely presented by the scalar presentation $E^0\to E^{r_j}\to P_j\to0$, and coordinatewise multiplication identifies $\Lambda_{W_j}\otimes_E P_j$ with $\Lambda_{W_j}^{r_j}$. Thus each stratum has a finite constant local model and the chosen stratification satisfies [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

source.place: Example 3.1 and Theorem 6.2(2)–(3); existing finite-field local-triviality bridge, then the scalar free model

proof.text: For the specified $\Lambda=\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}}_\ell$, start with a stratification witnessing [def-sfb-constructible-module]. On each stratum $S$ its restriction has local finite free cokernel presentations by [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality], using the Noetherian topology from step 2. That statement uses exactly the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]; it gives $M|_{W_j}\cong\Lambda_{W_j}^{r_j}$ on a pro-étale cover of $S$. The scalar ring is $\Lambda(*)=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$: every single algebraic element belongs to a finite subextension. Take $P_j=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^{r_j}$, with presentation from the zero module. The coordinatewise tensor identification of step 5 gives its finite constant model. The original stratification now satisfies [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

source.place: IsLocallyFinitelyPresented and IsConstructible; existing bounded-image algebraic-closure local-triviality bridge

proof.text: Steps 3–6 prove the module-predicate equivalence for the three specified coefficient families. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], an object $K$ of the ordinary $D_X$ belongs to $\mathcal B_X$ exactly when its cohomology vanishes outside an interval $[a,b]$ and every $H^n(K)$ has the first predicate. By [sk-def-sfb-constructible], membership in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ has the identical boundedness requirement and the second predicate for every $H^n(K)$. Substitute the proved equivalence degree by degree, retaining the same interval. The object properties, and hence their full subcategories with ambient morphisms, agree. Neither definition introduces derived completeness, so this argument needs no such condition.
